purpose: Bounded read-only latency sample for public Solana RPC and slot WebSocket access; not a PAPER bot soak.

http.request_order: JSON-RPC 2.0, IDs 1..40, order shuffled by Python random.Random(20261122), at least 1.0 s delay between sequential requests.
http.client: PowerShell here-string piped to Python 3.11; each request launched a fresh curl.exe process with --max-time 8 and an outer 10 s process timeout.
http.latency_definition: RTT is time.perf_counter around the curl subprocess, including process startup and fresh DNS/TCP/TLS/HTTP setup; curl time_total was parsed but not used for percentile calculations.
http.validation: All responses were HTTP 200 with valid JSON-RPC results; getHealth returned ok and getSlot returned an integer.
http.statistics: Successful RTTs only. Nearest-rank percentile ceil(p*n)-1; with n=10, p95 and p99 equal the maximum observation.

websocket.statistics: p95 and p99 use nearest-rank percentiles; with n=11 both equal the maximum interval.

limitations: The sample is short and unauthenticated; it does not represent the bot's configured aiohttp connection reuse, Helius enhanced feed, token event parsing, retries, confirmation paths, or sustained production reliability.
The HTTP request rows and WebSocket interval rows were not retained; only the aggregate values shown here are available. Individual sample values are not reconstructed.
Public RPC documentation says shared public endpoints are not intended for production use. These results are diagnostic only.
This is not a 24-hour PAPER soak and does not establish LIVE readiness.
